approvalRequirements: Be an eligible SoCalGas nonresidential customer with qualifying natural-gas service at the installation site.
Purchase and install new equipment that appears on the current business rebate schedule and meets the applicable efficiency, fuel, replacement, installation, and quantity requirements.
Complete the purchase and installation within the eligible program period and submit the current application by the stated deadline.
Provide a paid itemized invoice and the required account, site, manufacturer, model, efficiency, quantity, and installation information.

Permit SoCalGas or its program administrator to verify the customer, equipment, installation, and claimed costs, including an inspection when requested, and remain within program caps and available funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SoCalGas publishes prescriptive business equipment rebates with objective customer, equipment, installation, documentation, and timing rules rather than competitive scoring. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be paid after administrative review and any requested verification, subject to current measure availability, caps, and program funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Current SoCalGas business materials require eligible gas service, qualifying new equipment, a timely documented application, and program verification before rebate payment.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible SoCalGas nonresidential customer with an account and project that satisfy the current financing rules.
Use a qualifying energy-efficiency project that participates in an applicable SoCalGas rebate or incentive pathway and meets the program's technical, savings, payback, and financing limits.
Maintain an account in good standing and satisfy the program's repayment and creditworthiness requirements.
Submit the financing application, project scope, estimated costs, savings calculations, contractor information, and other required documents before purchasing or installing the measures.

Receive written project and financing approval, execute the financing agreement, complete the approved installation, and provide final invoices and verification records before loan funding or on-bill repayment begins.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The zero-percent financing pathway requires advance technical review, customer and repayment qualification, an approved energy-efficiency project, and available first-come program funds. A conforming project can be financed, but approval is not automatic because underwriting, project economics, meter-level limits, and budget availability materially affect the decision.
reviews.evidenceText: SoCalGas currently requires eligible business service, an approved qualifying efficiency project, advance financing review, executed loan documents, and completed-project verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible SoCalGas residential customer and install the equipment at a qualifying existing residence served by SoCalGas.
Purchase and install a product that is currently listed for a residential rebate and meets the applicable fuel, product, efficiency, installation, and replacement requirements.
Complete the purchase and installation within the current eligibility period before submitting the claim.
Submit the rebate application with the customer and installation-site information, itemized receipt or invoice, model number, and required product-label or installation photographs.
Allow SoCalGas or its administrator to validate the account, equipment, installation, and documentation and to inspect the installation when requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The residential offering is a rules-based rebate process, not a competitive award. An eligible customer with a currently qualifying natural-gas product and a complete documented claim is likely to receive the rebate after validation, subject to measure limits and available program funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Current SoCalGas residential materials direct customers to install a qualifying product and submit a documented claim that remains subject to account, product, and installation verification.

approvalRequirements: Own or control the environmental attributes of a qualifying solar facility that satisfies Pennsylvania Alternative Energy Portfolio Standards eligibility and geographic rules.
Create a PennAEPS account and submit a complete facility-certification application with ownership, equipment, capacity, location, interconnection, placed-in-service, and metering documentation.
Receive a Pennsylvania alternative-energy-system certification number for the facility.
Register the certified facility in PJM Generation Attribute Tracking System and establish compliant revenue-quality metering and generation reporting.
Report generation accurately, preserve credit ownership records, and comply with transfer, retirement, audit, and continuing-certification requirements.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Facility certification and credit creation are administrative, rules-based processes. A qualifying solar facility with complete documentation and compliant metering is likely to be certified and generate credits; selling the credits is optional, and neither a buyer nor a market price is guaranteed.
reviews.evidenceText: Pennsylvania's current AEPS process requires facility certification and PJM-GATS registration before verified solar generation can create alternative energy credits.

approvalRequirements: Purchase a solar energy system or component that falls within Florida's current statutory sales-tax exemption and applicable certification rules.
Ensure the seller applies the exemption only to qualifying solar equipment and separately accounts for taxable items or services when required.
Provide any purchaser certificate or representation requested by the seller and retain invoices, component descriptions, certifications, and installation records for audit.
Do not treat ordinary HVAC, boiler, combined-heat-and-power, fuel-cell, or standalone storage equipment as eligible unless it independently satisfies the current solar-system exemption.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Florida's current solar-equipment sales-tax exemption is statutory and ordinarily applies at the sale when the purchased property meets the legal definition and documentation rules. The current official law does not substantiate a general exemption for the title's broad CHP and conventional-equipment mappings, so those items should not be assumed eligible.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Florida law provides a point-of-sale exemption for qualifying solar energy systems and components; it does not establish a general sales-tax exemption for ordinary CHP, HVAC, boiler, fuel-cell, or standalone-storage equipment under this record.

approvalRequirements: Own the residential property where the eligible energy or resilience improvement will be installed and be located in a state and area currently served by SELF.
Include all required property titleholders and, where applicable, a spouse in the application and loan documents.
Provide income, identity, housing-payment, property-tax, mortgage, debt, and other records needed to establish ability to repay and program eligibility.
Use an eligible project scope, contractor, and written proposal that satisfy SELF's current product and underwriting requirements.
Receive final credit and project approval, execute the loan documents, and comply with contractor-disbursement, completion, and verification requirements.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SELF does not rely solely on a minimum credit score, but it conducts full ability-to-repay, property, borrower, contractor, and project underwriting. A qualifying improvement may receive financing, while household finances, existing obligations, title issues, project suitability, and final underwriting can still result in denial or changed terms.
reviews.evidenceText: SELF currently finances qualifying residential solar, battery, and energy improvements only after borrower ability-to-repay, property, contractor, and project review.

approvalRequirements: Be a Hawaii business taxpayer that owns and places a qualifying solar or wind energy system in service in Hawaii.
Meet the current technology, system-output, eligible-cost, placed-in-service, credit-cap, and any utility or permitting requirements applicable to the system.
Complete Form N-342 and any required Form N-342A or N-342C schedules, certifications, and cost-allocation worksheets.
Claim the allowable credit on the applicable Hawaii corporate income-tax return and observe carryover, refundable-credit election, basis, and recapture rules.
Retain contracts, invoices, proof of payment, permits, interconnection records, specifications, and placed-in-service documentation for Department of Taxation review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The Renewable Energy Technologies Income Tax Credit is a statutory, noncompetitive tax benefit with no current repeal date. A corporate taxpayer that places a qualifying system in service, computes the credit correctly, and files the required forms should receive the allowable credit through ordinary return processing, subject to audit and statutory caps.
reviews.evidenceText: Hawaii's current corporate forms include the renewable-energy credit schedules, and the Department of Taxation states that the statutory credit currently has no repeal date.

approvalRequirements: Be a Hawaii individual taxpayer that owns and places a qualifying solar or wind energy system in service in Hawaii.
Meet the current technology, system-output, eligible-cost, placed-in-service, credit-cap, and any utility or permitting requirements applicable to the system.
Complete Form N-342 and any required Form N-342A or N-342C schedules, certifications, and cost-allocation worksheets.
Claim the allowable credit on the applicable Hawaii individual income-tax return and observe carryover, refundable-credit election, basis, and recapture rules.
Retain contracts, invoices, proof of payment, permits, interconnection records, specifications, and placed-in-service documentation for Department of Taxation review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The Renewable Energy Technologies Income Tax Credit is a statutory, noncompetitive tax benefit with no current repeal date. An individual taxpayer that places a qualifying system in service, computes the credit correctly, and files the required forms should receive the allowable credit through ordinary return processing, subject to audit and statutory caps.
reviews.evidenceText: Hawaii's current individual forms include the renewable-energy credit schedules, and the Department of Taxation states that the statutory credit currently has no repeal date.

approvalRequirements: Purchase property that meets Arizona's statutory definition of a solar energy device, which includes specified systems that collect, transfer, or store solar energy and qualifying wind-generator systems.
Purchase from or use a retailer or solar-energy contractor registered with the Arizona Department of Revenue as required for the applicable retail or use-tax treatment.
Have the seller or contractor apply the statutory retail tax-base deduction or use-tax exemption to the qualifying device and separately state taxable property or services when required.
Retain the invoice, equipment description, seller or contractor information, and installation records sufficient to substantiate the exemption in an audit.
Do not claim submetering or monitoring equipment as a standalone exempt device unless it is an integral qualifying component of the covered energy system.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Arizona's treatment is statutory and noncompetitive. A purchase of a qualifying solar energy device, including a wind-generator system within the statutory definition, from the required registered seller or contractor should receive the tax treatment at the transaction, subject to correct classification and audit.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Arizona statutes provide retail and use-tax treatment for qualifying solar energy devices and expressly include qualifying wind-generator systems in the governing definition.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pennsylvania business, economic-development organization, political subdivision, or other applicant class allowed by the current Alternative and Clean Energy Program.
Propose an eligible Pennsylvania alternative-energy, clean-energy, energy-efficiency, or energy-conservation project and limit the request to eligible costs.

Provide the required applicant match, application fee, project budget, financing plan, technical studies, site-control records, permits, schedules, ownership information, and economic or energy-impact documentation.
Avoid beginning disqualifying project work or incurring ineligible costs before the applicable program authorization.
Receive Commonwealth Financing Authority approval and satisfy commitment, closing, security, reporting, and continuing-compliance conditions.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current official pathway is the broader Alternative and Clean Energy Program, under which grants and loans are reviewed and approved by the Commonwealth Financing Authority. Eligible solar-related projects may compete for assistance, but approval is discretionary and depends on project merits, match, documentation, financing, and available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Pennsylvania's current official source identifies the Alternative and Clean Energy Program, not a separate stand-alone Solar Energy Incentives Program, and requires a complete application and Commonwealth Financing Authority approval.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pennsylvania business, economic-development organization, political subdivision, or other applicant class allowed by the Solar Energy Program.
Propose an eligible Pennsylvania solar generation, solar-use, or solar-equipment-manufacturing project and limit the loan request to eligible costs.
Provide at least one dollar of applicant match for each three dollars of requested loan assistance and pay the current application fee.
Submit complete technical, financial, ownership, site-control, permitting, project-cost, repayment, collateral, and schedule documentation before project authorization.
Receive Commonwealth Financing Authority loan approval, pay the applicable commitment fee, execute closing and security documents, and comply with disbursement, reporting, and performance conditions.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Solar Energy Program loans require a complete preproject application, borrower and project financial review, match, security, and a discretionary Commonwealth Financing Authority decision. A well-supported eligible project can be approved, but the loan is not automatic and remains dependent on underwriting, authority approval, and available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Pennsylvania's current Solar Energy Program offers project loans through a matched, fee-based application that requires Commonwealth Financing Authority approval and loan closing.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pennsylvania business, economic-development organization, political subdivision, or other applicant class allowed by the Solar Energy Program.
Propose an eligible Pennsylvania solar generation, solar-use, or solar-equipment-manufacturing project and limit the grant request to eligible costs.
Provide at least one dollar of applicant match for each dollar of requested grant assistance and pay the current application fee.
Submit complete technical, financial, ownership, site-control, permitting, project-cost, schedule, public-benefit, and energy-production documentation before project authorization.

Receive a Commonwealth Financing Authority grant award, execute the commitment and grant agreement, transfer solar renewable energy credits when required for grant-funded photovoltaic generation, and comply with reporting and performance conditions.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Solar Energy Program grants are discretionary, matched awards requiring a complete preproject application and Commonwealth Financing Authority approval. An eligible, well-documented project may receive funding, but competitive demand, public benefit, match, project readiness, and available funds materially affect the outcome.
reviews.evidenceText: Pennsylvania's current Solar Energy Program offers matched grants for eligible solar projects only after application review and Commonwealth Financing Authority approval.

approvalRequirements: Purchase a system that meets Minnesota's statutory definition of a solar energy system, including the qualifying equipment and integral components covered by the exemption.
Have the seller apply the sales-tax exemption to the qualifying system and separately account for taxable nonqualifying property or services.
Provide a completed exemption certificate when the seller requests one.
Retain the purchase agreement, invoice, system description, component records, and installation documentation for Minnesota Department of Revenue review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Minnesota's solar-energy-system sales-tax exemption is statutory and noncompetitive. A transaction that consists of qualifying solar equipment and is properly documented should receive the exemption at the sale, subject to seller classification and Department of Revenue audit.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Minnesota law exempts qualifying solar energy systems from sales tax, with the seller administering the transaction and retaining exemption documentation.

approvalRequirements: Own qualifying personal property located in the District of Columbia that is a system using exclusively solar energy or a cogeneration system meeting the statutory definition.
Classify only qualifying system property as exempt and exclude ordinary equipment that is not part of the covered solar or cogeneration system.
Report the property and claimed exemption accurately on Form FP-31 when a personal-property return is otherwise required and file through MyTax.DC.gov by the applicable deadline.
Retain ownership, location, cost, equipment, operating-use, production, installation, and placed-in-service records for Office of Tax and Revenue review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current District law provides a statutory personal-property tax exemption, rather than a discretionary credit, for qualifying exclusively solar and cogeneration systems. A taxpayer that correctly classifies and reports qualifying property should receive the exemption through ordinary tax administration, subject to audit.
reviews.evidenceText: District law currently exempts qualifying exclusively solar and cogeneration systems from personal-property tax, while the annual FP-31 process remains subject to Office of Tax and Revenue review.

approvalRequirements: Be a South Carolina corporate taxpayer that owns and installs a qualifying solar-energy, small-hydropower, or geothermal-energy property in South Carolina.
Use the system for a qualifying statutory purpose such as water heating, space heating, air cooling, daylighting, heat reclamation, demand response, or electricity generation.
Meet the applicable technical, certification, placed-in-service, eligible-cost, credit-percentage, annual-cap, and carryforward rules.
Complete Form TC-38 and attach or retain the required system certifications, cost calculations, invoices, and placed-in-service information.
Claim the allowable credit on the corporate income-tax return and retain documentation for Department of Revenue review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: South Carolina's credit is statutory and noncompetitive. A corporate taxpayer with a qualifying solar, small-hydropower, or geothermal system and a correctly completed TC-38 should receive the allowable credit through normal return processing, subject to annual limits, carryforward rules, and audit; ordinary controls or HVAC qualify only when part of a covered energy system.
reviews.evidenceText: Current South Carolina law and tax forms provide a post-installation income-tax credit for qualifying solar, small-hydropower, and geothermal systems, subject to system-use, certification, cap, and filing rules.

approvalRequirements: Be a South Carolina individual taxpayer that owns and installs a qualifying solar-energy, small-hydropower, or geothermal-energy property in South Carolina.
Use the system for a qualifying statutory purpose such as water heating, space heating, air cooling, daylighting, heat reclamation, demand response, or electricity generation.
Meet the applicable technical, certification, placed-in-service, eligible-cost, credit-percentage, annual-cap, and carryforward rules.
Complete Form TC-38 and attach or retain the required system certifications, cost calculations, invoices, and placed-in-service information.
Claim the allowable credit on the individual income-tax return and retain documentation for Department of Revenue review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: South Carolina's credit is statutory and noncompetitive. An individual taxpayer with a qualifying solar, small-hydropower, or geothermal system and a correctly completed TC-38 should receive the allowable credit through normal return processing, subject to annual limits, carryforward rules, and audit; ordinary controls or HVAC qualify only when part of a covered energy system.
reviews.evidenceText: Current South Carolina law and tax forms provide a post-installation income-tax credit for qualifying solar, small-hydropower, and geothermal systems, subject to system-use, certification, cap, and filing rules.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pennsylvania public school entity and own or control the school facility where the project will be installed.
Propose an eligible photovoltaic or solar-thermal project, including eligible energy storage and related equipment where permitted by current guidelines.
Complete the required energy, site, structural, design, cost, financing, match, schedule, procurement, and public-benefit analysis and provide site-control documentation.
Obtain or demonstrate a credible path to required permits, utility interconnection, inspections, and other project approvals.
Submit a complete application during an active funding round and receive Department of Community and Economic Development and Commonwealth Financing Authority approval.
Execute the grant agreement and comply with procurement, prevailing-wage or labor requirements when applicable, construction, reporting, reimbursement, inspection, and performance obligations.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Solar for Schools is a discretionary grant program with defined applicant and project rules but limited appropriations and Commonwealth Financing Authority approval. A ready, eligible school project can receive an award in an active round, while application timing, match, project quality, competing demand, and available funds prevent an assured outcome.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Pennsylvania materials restrict the program to eligible school entities and solar projects and require a complete round-specific application, authority approval, and grant-agreement compliance.

approvalRequirements: Develop an eligible Massachusetts solar photovoltaic project interconnected to a participating Eversource, National Grid, or Unitil distribution company and meet the current SMART 3.0 technology, site, ownership, sizing, and program rules.

Submit a PowerClerk Statement of Qualification application with the application fee and required site-control, interconnection, permitting, ownership, equipment, land-use, production, and adder documentation.
Avoid prohibited significant physical work before preliminary qualification where the current rules impose that restriction.
Receive a Preliminary Statement of Qualification, reserve the applicable capacity and compensation rate, and complete the project within the reservation period.
Install and interconnect the approved project, obtain permission to operate, establish compliant metering, and submit final as-built, interconnection, production, and energy-storage documentation.
Receive a Final Statement of Qualification after the applicable distribution-company tariff and payment mechanism are effective and maintain ongoing metering, reporting, and program compliance.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SMART 3.0 is accepting applications and issuing preliminary qualifications, but the current official program page states that the tariff term begins only after distribution-company tariff approval and a Final Statement of Qualification. A conforming project can reserve eligibility, while final qualification and payment remain dependent on project completion, utility implementation, and final program review.
reviews.evidenceText: Massachusetts currently accepts SMART 3.0 qualification applications and uses preliminary and final qualification stages; the incentive term starts only after the applicable tariff is approved and final qualification is issued.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible nonresidential customer of Portland General Electric or Pacific Power in Oregon with a proposed solar or battery-storage project covered by the current Energy Trust development-assistance offering.
Work through an eligible Energy Trust solar trade ally and create the separate PowerClerk development-assistance project before beginning the reimbursable study or planning work.
Submit the required project, customer, site, utility, system concept, contractor, scope, cost, and incentive-reservation information.
Complete a qualifying feasibility or development report addressing resource, design, economics, permitting, interconnection, siting, and other required technical topics and provide the paid invoice.
Receive Energy Trust technical review and final approval of the development-assistance project before reimbursement.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Solar Development Assistance and Battery Storage Development Assistance offerings reimburse defined planning costs through a published PowerClerk and technical-review process rather than competitive scoring. A timely reserved study that meets the report and invoice requirements is likely to be approved, subject to customer eligibility and available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Energy Trust's current development-assistance offerings replace the legacy Solar Planning title and require advance PowerClerk reservation, an eligible trade ally, a qualifying study, invoice documentation, and technical approval.

approvalRequirements: Own or control the renewable attributes of a solar resource that satisfies Maryland Renewable Portfolio Standard technology, location, interconnection, and placed-in-service requirements.

Submit a complete Maryland Public Service Commission renewable-energy-facility certification application with ownership, system, capacity, location, interconnection, metering, and placed-in-service records.
Receive a Maryland renewable-energy-facility certification number for the solar resource.
Register the certified facility in PJM Generation Attribute Tracking System and establish compliant metering and generation reporting.
For on-site or behind-the-meter generation, submit the required Maryland generation reports and maintain credit ownership, transfer, retirement, and audit records.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Maryland certification and credit creation are rules-based administrative processes. A qualifying solar resource with complete documentation and compliant metering is likely to be certified and create SRECs; registration does not guarantee a buyer or market price, and non-solar monitoring equipment alone is not an eligible resource.
reviews.evidenceText: Maryland currently requires Public Service Commission facility certification and PJM-GATS registration before verified qualifying solar generation can create SRECs.

approvalRequirements: Own or control the renewable attributes of a solar facility that meets District of Columbia Renewable Portfolio Standard technology and geographic or feeder requirements.
Submit the Commission's current online certification application with ownership, location, equipment, capacity, as-built, interconnection, permission-to-operate, and metering documentation.
Receive a District of Columbia Public Service Commission certification order or facility number.
Register the certified facility in PJM Generation Attribute Tracking System and establish compliant meter reading and generation reporting.
Maintain geographic eligibility, renewable-attribute ownership, transfer, retirement, and continuing-compliance records.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: District certification and SREC creation use published eligibility and documentation rules. A qualifying facility with complete as-built, interconnection, and metering records is likely to be certified and create credits, while credit sales and market value remain separate and are not guaranteed.
reviews.evidenceText: The District's current RPS process requires Commission certification and PJM-GATS registration before qualifying solar generation can create District-eligible SRECs.

approvalRequirements: Own the SRECs from a qualifying Delaware-interconnected or otherwise eligible solar photovoltaic facility that has completed the required state and PJM-GATS registration and metering steps.
Submit a valid bid or application during an open SREC Delaware procurement or spot-market window and satisfy the applicable ownership, system-tier, vintage, quantity, and documentation rules.
Accept the applicable procurement or auction terms if the bid is selected.
Transfer the offered SRECs in PJM Generation Attribute Tracking System using the required Spot Market or other specified transfer type and meet the stated transfer deadline.
Maintain facility, ownership, generation, transfer, and payment records and comply with program verification and contract obligations.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current SREC Delaware structure includes operational instructions for transferring credits through procurement and spot-market processes, but bid selection, clearing price, eligible volume, and the timing of open windows are competitive or market-dependent. A valid eligible bid may be accepted, but an award is not assured.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Delaware materials administer SREC purchases through procurement and spot-market transfer procedures, with bid acceptance and price dependent on the active solicitation and market results.

approvalRequirements: For the mapped battery measure, purchase qualifying residential energy-storage-system equipment installed in or on a New York residence during the statutory June 1, 2024 through May 31, 2028 exemption period.
Ensure the seller applies the state and applicable local sales-tax exemption only to qualifying equipment and installation services and separately accounts for taxable items.
Retain the contract, invoice, system specifications, residence and installation records, and any exemption certificate requested by the seller.

For a claim under the separate solar-equipment exemption, demonstrate that the property is qualifying residential or commercial solar-energy equipment or an integral component of that system rather than standalone commercial storage.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: New York currently provides a statutory sales-tax exemption for qualifying residential energy-storage equipment and installation through May 31, 2028, and a separate exemption for qualifying solar-energy systems. A properly classified residential battery transaction should receive the exemption at the sale, but the legacy Solar Sales Tax Exemption title does not establish a general exemption for standalone commercial batteries.
reviews.evidenceText: Current New York guidance separately exempts qualifying solar equipment and qualifying residential energy-storage equipment; the temporary residential storage exemption runs through May 31, 2028.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Hawaii Energy residential electric ratepayer on Hawaii Island, Lanai, Maui, Molokai, or Oahu; Kauai customers are not served by this program.

Install a new qualifying solar-thermal water-heating system or an approved photovoltaic-direct water-heating system that meets current equipment, sizing, installation, warranty, and customer requirements.
Use a participating Hawaii Energy residential solar-water-heating contractor.
Have the contractor apply the instant rebate to the customer invoice and submit the required customer, utility-account, equipment, installation, invoice, and completion documentation.
Permit Hawaii Energy to verify or inspect the installation and apply while the current first-come program budget remains available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Hawaii Energy publishes an instant, contractor-delivered rebate with objective customer, territory, system, and installation requirements. A qualifying project completed by a participating contractor is likely to receive the invoice credit after program submission and verification, subject to current funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Hawaii Energy currently offers an instant residential solar-water-heating rebate through participating contractors for eligible ratepayers on the program's five covered island service areas.

approvalRequirements: Own and occupy an eligible Oregon home served by Portland General Electric or Pacific Power and satisfy the current Solar Within Reach customer rules.
For installations completed on or after June 1, 2026, document household income at or below 150 percent of the applicable area median income and complete the required income-verification process.

Install a qualifying customer-owned solar photovoltaic system, and any eligible paired battery, that meets current equipment, design, interconnection, permitting, warranty, and ownership requirements.
Use an Energy Trust solar trade ally and have the trade ally submit and reserve the incentive in PowerClerk before installation or other disqualifying project activity.

Execute the customer agreement, complete installation in the eligible program period, obtain jurisdictional approval and utility interconnection, and submit invoices, photos, inspection records, and final closeout documents.
Allow Energy Trust verification and remain within the applicable utility, project, household, incentive-step, and available-funding limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Solar Within Reach uses published income, utility, ownership, trade-ally, system, reservation, and closeout rules rather than competitive ranking. A qualifying household with a properly reserved and completed project is likely to receive the incentive after verification, subject to the current incentive step and available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Energy Trust's current 2026 materials require an eligible PGE or Pacific Power household, income qualification, a trade-ally PowerClerk reservation, qualifying customer-owned equipment, and final installation verification.
